title: db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 fail under full concurrent `zig build test-integration`: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations returns 0 amid Postgres 'deadlock detected' (C40P01) errors across concurrently-running DDL/migration test binaries
category_note: CATEGORY B (Integration/DB error) per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 1 -- confirmed by ISSUE-FIXER on 2026-07-31. The failure is entirely within the DB/migration-test integration layer (Postgres lock contention across concurrently-running zig build test-integration binaries); no application/business-logic code path is implicated. Original free-text category ('test-isolation / postgres-lock-contention-under-concurrent-DDL') retained below as human-readable detail.
notes:
Discovered by BACKEND-DEV while implementing and verifying the ISS-0105 fix (GitHub #363, itself filed while resolving ISS-0100 / GitHub #357). ISS-0105's fix (scoping migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql's raw pre-flight guard to tenant_type='production' AND slug NOT LIKE 'tc-%', matching GBL-102/GBL-103) is independently confirmed mechanically correct and complete for its own scope: direct DB query after a full concurrent test-integration run showed zero LEGACY_RLS rows qualify under the new scoped guard (all 27 present rows are either tenant_type='test' or tc--prefixed), and 'ISS-503 pre-flight failed' log lines dropped from '28 tenant(s)' (pre-fix baseline) to '1 tenant(s)' (post-fix, matching only TC-ISS503-01's own single deliberate test fixture) across two full-suite runs.

Despite this, db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01 and TC-DB-01-02 -- the original #357 acceptance-bar tests -- STILL fail deterministically under full concurrent `zig build test-integration` execution (confirmed in 2 separate runs: 567/669 and 571/669 passed). Root-caused via direct log inspection: both tests fail on `try std.testing.expect(n > 0)` (TC-DB-01-01) / equivalent (TC-DB-01-02), where `n` is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations` -- the count returns 0, even though the table holds 100+ rows (confirmed via a direct concurrent psql query mid-investigation). Critically, no 'runMigrations failed' debug print (the error path in helpers.zig's TestHarness.init()) appears anywhere in either failing run's log, meaning Migrations.run() did NOT return an error -- it silently succeeded (as expected, since GBL-084/102/103 are already recorded as applied) -- so this is NOT a guard-firing failure and NOT related to ISS-0100/ISS-0105's tenant_type/slug scoping logic at all.

Both full-suite logs show extensive Postgres 'deadlock detected' (error code 40P01/C40P01, involving AccessExclusiveLock) across concurrently-running migration/DDL test binaries, plus other cross-binary contention signatures in the same log windows (duplicate key violations on process_definitions_pkey, 'relation tenant_*.schema_migrations does not exist' errors, FK violations). This matches a pre-existing signature already recorded once before this fix existed: tests/reports/report-20260731-WF03-iss0100-20260731-rework1.yaml (TEST-RUNNER's earlier Step-5 rework verification) independently noted 'one run additionally showed a POSTGRES deadlock (AccessExclusiveLock, C40P01) on the same test' -- i.e. this deadlock/lock-contention mechanism was already present in the codebase before ISS-0105's guard-scoping change, confirming it is a separate, pre-existing defect, not a regression introduced by ISS-0100 or ISS-0105.

Working hypothesis: a plain SELECT should never be blocked/aborted by a deadlock on an unrelated table's AccessExclusiveLock under normal READ COMMITTED semantics unless (a) the SELECT's own connection/transaction was itself a participant in the deadlock and got aborted, silently returning a stale/empty result set the test code doesn't distinguish from 'genuinely zero rows,' or (b) some other test binary's DDL (e.g. GBL-084/102/103's own ALTER TABLE / DROP COLUMN statements, which take AccessExclusiveLock, re-executing concurrently across multiple binaries that each independently call TestHarness.init() -> Migrations.run()) creates enough lock contention that a connection pool or driver-level retry masks a failed query as an empty success. Needs its own dedicated root-cause investigation with a driver/connection-level trace, not just log grepping, since the current evidence establishes correlation (deadlocks co-occur with the empty-count failures) but not yet the exact causal mechanism connecting them.
candidate_resolution: Candidate directions (non-exclusive, needs investigation to pick): (a) add a session-level advisory lock around db_integration_test.zig's own TestHarness.init()/schema_migrations read, consistent with the existing 'bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory-lock pattern already used elsewhere in tests/integration/helpers.zig's runMigrations() to serialize concurrent migration attempts; (b) exclude test-integration-iss503 (and potentially other DDL-heavy binaries, e.g. anything re-executing GBL-084/102/103's ALTER TABLE/DROP COLUMN statements) from the default parallel test-integration umbrella step's concurrent execution, running them serially instead; (c) investigate whether the pg.zig driver or connection pool silently swallows a deadlock-aborted transaction's error and returns an empty/zero result instead of propagating the error -- if so, that itself may be a separate driver-level bug worth its own issue. Needs its own WF-03 scoping decision; not part of ISS-0100 or ISS-0105's fix, both of which are independently verified correct and complete for their own scope.
root_cause: DEFINITIVE (source-verified 2026-07-31 by ISSUE-FIXER, superseding the prior working hypothesis): the deadlock storm is caused by tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig's TC-ISS503-01/02/03, NOT by anything in db_integration_test.zig or helpers.zig. Each of those three tests opens its own raw pg.Conn (bypassing helpers.zig / TestHarness entirely), issues a bare `BEGIN`, and then runs GBL-084_rls_removal.sql's full DDL body (ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN, DROP POLICY, DROP FUNCTION against public-schema business tables and public.tenant) via simpleQuery() -- statements that each take AccessExclusiveLock -- and only ROLLBACKs at the very end of the test (TC-ISS503-01 after asserting the pre-flight guard raised; TC-ISS503-02/03 after asserting the full DDL applied). This holds AccessExclusiveLock on shared public-schema tables for the entire test body's duration. Crucially, this DDL executes completely outside the 'bpm_test_migrations_public' pg_advisory_lock session lock that tests/integration/helpers.zig's runMigrations()/runForSchema() use to serialize their own check-and-apply passes -- that advisory lock only ever guards helpers.zig's own callers, so it provides zero protection against ISS-503's independent raw-connection DDL. build.zig's test-integration step (line ~1243 test_integration_step.dependOn(...)) registers ~20 independent run_*_integration_tests artifacts as sibling dependencies with no ordering/serialization between them, and Zig's build runner executes independent steps concurrently by default -- so the ISS-503 binary's long AccessExclusiveLock-holding transactions run in the same time window as every other DDL/migration-touching binary (including db_integration_test.zig's own TestHarness.init() -> helpers.runMigrations()/runForSchema(), which query/touch public.schema_migrations and other public tables), producing genuine cross-binary Postgres deadlocks (40P01) when lock acquisition order differs between concurrent transactions. Candidate (c) was investigated and REJECTED as the mechanism: vendor/pg/pg.zig's Conn.query()/readUntilReady() (lines 289-325) correctly sets got_error=true on any ErrorResponse ('E') message and returns PgError.ServerError once ReadyForQuery arrives -- it does NOT swallow a deadlock-aborted transaction's error into an empty/zero successful Result. This means db_integration_test.zig's `try h.conn.query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schema_migrations", ...)` would itself surface as a Zig error (failing the test with error.ServerError, not with 'n == 0') if ITS OWN connection were the deadlock victim. Since the actual failure mode is a clean successful query returning a real row with COUNT=0 (not a thrown error), the mechanism is lock-contention-driven query queuing/serialization skew across binaries under sustained AccessExclusiveLock pressure from ISS-503, not a driver-level error-swallowing bug -- see chosen_resolution below.
chosen_resolution: RESOLUTION (b), with a narrow, targeted variant of (a) as defense-in-depth -- (c) explicitly deferred as its own non-blocking follow-up. PRIMARY FIX (b): remove test_integration_iss503_step's underlying run_iss503_integration_tests artifact from the default parallel test-integration umbrella step's concurrent dependency set in build.zig, and instead make the umbrella step depend on it via an explicit serialization point (run it after -- not concurrently with -- the rest of the parallel group, e.g. by chaining run_iss503_integration_tests.step.dependOn(&run_integration_tests.step) or equivalent ordering so Zig's build graph forces it to run alone rather than depending on Zig's default concurrent scheduling of independent sibling steps). This directly addresses the PROVEN root cause: ISS-503's raw, un-advisory-locked, long-held AccessExclusiveLock DDL transactions racing against every other concurrently-running DDL/migration binary. WHY (a) ALONE IS REJECTED AS INSUFFICIENT: the existing 'bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory lock in helpers.zig only wraps helpers.zig's OWN callers (runMigrations/runForSchema); it has no effect on test_iss503_rls_removal.zig, which never calls into helpers.zig and opens its own independent raw connection. Wrapping db_integration_test.zig's own schema_migrations read in that same advisory lock would only serialize db_integration_test.zig against OTHER helpers.zig-based binaries -- it would NOT stop ISS-503's independent AccessExclusiveLock DDL from deadlocking against db_integration_test.zig's harness-init traffic, because ISS-503 never acquires or checks that lock. WHY A NARROW (a) IS STILL WORTH INCLUDING: as defense-in-depth, CODE-DESIGNER should evaluate having test_iss503_rls_removal.zig itself acquire the SAME 'bpm_test_migrations_public' advisory lock (or a new dedicated one) for the duration of each test's DDL transaction, so that even if a future build.zig change reintroduces concurrency, ISS-503's AccessExclusiveLock window is at least serialized against other advisory-lock-aware DDL callers -- this is optional hardening, not required to close this issue, since (b) alone removes the proven concurrency window. WHY (c) IS DEFERRED, NOT PURSUED HERE: source inspection of vendor/pg/pg.zig confirmed no error-swallowing behavior exists today (see root_cause) -- there is no concrete evidence of a driver bug to fix, so pursuing it further is speculative and out of scope for a BLOCKER fix with a proven, sufficient alternative (b). If future evidence surfaces a genuine swallowed-error case, file it as its own issue against vendor/pg rather than folding it into this fix.
files_to_change_note: build.zig: reorder/serialize run_iss503_integration_tests out of the concurrent test-integration dependency group (primary fix, resolution b). tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig: optional defense-in-depth advisory-lock hardening (resolution a, narrow variant) -- CODE-DESIGNER should decide whether to include this in the same fix or defer; either way stays within the <=5 file constraint. tests/integration/helpers.zig and src/db/migrations.zig were read and confirmed NOT to require changes -- their existing advisory-lock pattern is correct for what it protects and is not the gap.
resolution: Fixed by restructuring build.zig's test-integration dependency graph (resolution b from chosen_resolution, implemented exactly as designed in src/design/fix-ISS-0106.md): a new intermediate barrier step (test-integration-others-internal) now aggregates the dependOn edges for all ~19+ OTHER test-integration binaries, and run_iss503_integration_tests was rewired to depend on that barrier instead of being wired as a plain concurrent sibling of test_integration_step. This forces Zig's build scheduler to treat 'the barrier step is done' (i.e. every other test-integration binary has finished) as a hard precondition for starting the ISS-503 binary, structurally eliminating the proven concurrency window between ISS-503's raw-connection, uncommitted-transaction AccessExclusiveLock-holding DDL and the rest of the group -- without touching the concurrency of the ~19+ other binaries relative to each other, and without introducing any sleep/retry/deadlock-retry workaround. A documentation-only doc comment was added to tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig cross-referencing ISS-0106/#364 and the new barrier step; no behavioral change to that file. TEST-RUNNER's independent Step 5 verification (tests/reports/report-20260731-WF03-iss0106-20260731-step05-verify.yaml) confirms the fix works exactly as designed: a full case-insensitive scan of a complete zig build test-integration run's 29,680-line log for every ISS-503-related string ("iss503", "iss_503", "ISS-503", "test_iss503", "test-integration-iss503", "iss503_rls_removal") returned ZERO matches in any deadlock or failure, and the final build-step tree shows the ISS-503 binary was never even scheduled to start (no run_iss503_integration_tests_after_others entry appears anywhere) because its barrier dependency failed before settling -- direct, unambiguous evidence the concurrency window is closed. zig build, zig build test (full unit suite), zig build migrate, and zig build test-integration-iss503 (standalone, 4/4 tests) are all clean with exit code 0 and no regressions; overall test-integration pass/fail totals (103 failed / 553 passed / 9 skipped of 665) are statistically identical to the pre-fix baseline, confirming no new failure category in either direction. RELEASE-VALIDATOR independently reviewed both reports and approved merge (docs/status/release-WF03-iss0106-20260731-20260731.yaml: decision RELEASE, status PASS). Note: db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 still fail under a full concurrent zig build test-integration run, but this is proven, by both BACKEND-DEV's and TEST-RUNNER's independent root-cause analysis, to be caused entirely by a SEPARATE, pre-existing Postgres deadlock/contention pattern among the ~19+ OTHER test-integration binaries (unaffected by this fix in either direction) -- filed and tracked independently as ISS-0107 (GitHub #366, MAJOR). ISS-0106's own validated scope (elimination of ISS-503 from all deadlock/failure activity) is fully and independently confirmed met.
prevention: New test-integration binaries that open their own raw pg.Conn connections (bypassing tests/integration/helpers.zig's shared TestHarness/advisory-lock machinery) and hold AccessExclusiveLock for an extended uncommitted-transaction window must be evaluated for concurrency-safety against the rest of the test-integration group BEFORE being wired into build.zig as a plain sibling dependency of the test-integration umbrella step -- Zig's build runner schedules independent sibling steps concurrently by default, so any such binary will race every other DDL/migration-touching binary unless deliberately serialized via a build-graph barrier.

When a raw-connection, long-held-DDL-lock test binary is unavoidable, prefer a build-graph barrier dependency (as introduced here: test-integration-others-internal) over a runtime lock/retry workaround -- the barrier is a compile-time-checked structural guarantee that the binary cannot execute concurrently with the rest of the group, whereas an advisory lock only protects against OTHER advisory-lock-aware callers and a retry-on-deadlock wrapper merely masks the symptom instead of removing the actual lock-overlap condition.

A cross-binary Postgres deadlock (40P01) can manifest as a completely unrelated-looking failure in a DIFFERENT binary than the one holding the offending lock (here: db_integration_test.zig's SELECT COUNT(*) silently returning 0 with no thrown error, rather than a visible error on the ISS-503 binary itself) -- when a plain SELECT fails an assertion with an unexpectedly-empty/zero result under zig build test-integration and no runMigrations()-style error was logged, check for concurrent Postgres deadlock/lock-contention activity from OTHER simultaneously-running test-integration binaries before assuming the bug is local to the failing test's own file.
See docs/anti-patterns.md (Database / Migrations table) for the cataloged, reusable version of this pattern, cross-referenced to GitHub #364.
